Note that the minimum PL of this spell is 2, one for the god spell effect and one for the original spell effect. God spells can leave permanent marks on the land, this is up to the GM to decide. Like plants may not grow or snow immediately melt on the spot where a “god spell fireball” landed, and so on.

Using this spell, you stir your victim’s blood and bring out strong emotions such as lust, fear or rage. The victim must give in to these emotions in some way – exactly how depends on the individual and the situation. The GM determines the details. The spell has no effect in combat and cannot be used against monsters.

system.ingredient: One of your things and one of the targets
system.description: You swap bodies with another target for a turn per PL and after that you both switch back. Each target gains the STR, AGI and appearance of their new body, but keeps all other attributes, skills and talents. An unwilling target may resist by making a successful insight roll with a penalty equal to the PL, but only as long as they are conscious. The switch back only happens if both bodies are alive, if they are not. The one that remains stays in their new form forever. If so their STR and AGI will move towards their old values with one point per week. You can only swap bodies with other living non-monster kin.
You can mediate to attune to the world once per QD. If you manage to mediate for a whole turn (15 minutes), you can set you WP to twice the PL, but never higher than your EMP.

You can use this spell to grant mental aid to your allies. Up to one ally per PL gains a +1 bonus die to a skill you select upon casting this spell for its duration. This counts as if you help their rolls, and is therefore limited to the normal rules for helping others. The effect ends if you lose consciousness.

You can meld two different beings’ substances together, creating a new amalgam being. This spell requires 1 unit of mog per PL. The other ingredient (needle and thread) only increases the PL. The target(s) must succeed an insight check to not go completely insane, and even on a success it permanently loses a point of EMP. The new creature can have a combined attribute score no higher than 4 times the PL.

system.ingredient: Blanket of insects (optional; consumed if available)
system.description: You open your mouth and vomits forth a stream of insects. This counts as a fear attack that deals PL damage to WIT, that can be split among any selected targets in the area. The spell has no effect on monsters. This spell creates a blanket of insects upon casting it.

You can briefly reduce another person’s WIT to zero, which renders them Broken (without suffering a critical injury) and incapable of rational thought. The victim must make an INSIGHT roll (not an action) with a negative modification equal to the PL to resist the spell. The roll cannot be pushed. Once the spell wears off the person recovers one point of WIT per round.
As long as you travel by foot, you and a party of up to 10 people, as long as they stay within S range of you, can travel one extra hex per QD, for one QD per PL.
Manipulating the element of Earth, you hurl stones and rocks at an enemy in combat. The damage (to STR) from your attack is equal to the PL. Armor works normally.
You may use an overturned tree, as a way of transport from one hex in a forest to any other hex in the same forest. The door accepts up to one person to walk through per PL.
This spell is cast together with a ritual. It reduces the time to cast a ritual from a QD to a Turn (15 minutes). Casting a Quickened Ritual is taxing, so you cannot do it more than once per QD.

system.ingredient: See Epic Magic (Epic Magic ingredients do not increase Power Level)
system.description:
Special: Epic Magic.

This is an Epic Spell, see the description for those in this booklet. Each PL requires an ingredient. This ritual must be cast at the same time as the artifact is created, most often through a crafting roll with an added -1 penalty per PL. If the roll is failed, the item shatters and the artifact is not created. If the roll is pushed the artifact will be corrupted. A magical mishap will also corrupt it. After determining the total PL. The resulting artifact can have several effects with a total cost up to the PL. Even though the players may wish for what the artifact should do, the GM has the final say and may tweak or corrupt any and particularly breaking combinations. All the listed effects are only examples, use your imagination to come up with more. FOR EACH PL: Artifact die: Added with item dice of a chosen skill or as armor. Can be added to a sub-skill, like only when using endurance to resist poison, or only when fighting undead, this increases the die category by 1. If enhancing a sub-usage and still keeping a bonus when not using that sub-usage, it increases cost by 0.5. Cost: 1 ([[/r 1d8]]), 2 ([[/r 1d10]]), 3 ([[/r 1d12]]). Minimum total PL of item: 2 ([[/r 1d8]]), 4 ([[/r 1d10]]), 8 ([[/r 1d12]]). Magical access: Grants access to a spell you know as if cast by a grimoire with a set PL and magical rank (extra ranks can be added to reduce magical dice and risk of mishap). It still costs WP to use. Cost: 0.5 per magical rank. Cost modifier: +0.5 if PL is variable. Cost modifier: -0.5 for it to be usable only once per QD. Minimum total cost: 0.5. Daily magic: The item can cast a spell you know once per day and provides the WP needed, without any risk of magical mishap. Cost per magical rank: 0.5. It provides 1 WP per X on a [[/r 1d8]]. You can upgrade to a [[/r 1d10]] for 0.5 or to a [[/r 1d12]] for 1, or pay 3 for +2 fixed PL. Minimum total cost: 1. Permanent magic: The item constantly affects the owner with a magical effect at PL 1, but only as long as the item is wielded/worn. Cost: 1 if it has a normal duration of a day or more, 2 if its normally duration is a QD, 3 if its normal duration is a turn, 5 if its normal duration is a round. Also costs 0.5 per rank of the spell, add +0.5 if the effect should be togglable. Is the spell circumstantial, i.e. more unlikely then likely to benefit you during a week of adventuring? Cost modifier: x0.5. Limited magic: The item can use magic a limited number of times and then breaks. Costs and works as daily magic, but can be used multiple times per day. Cost modifiers: x0.25 for 3 charges, x0.5 for it to roll a die on use, first break after rolling a, x0.75 for 10 charges. Regenerating: The artifact cannot be repaired. It instead regenerates 1 item die every day, even if it is broken, as long as all the pieces are held together in place. Cost: 1. Indestructible: The artifact cannot lose item dice. It can only be destroyed via a reversal of this spell, including new ingredients or by other specific means. Cost: 2. Minimum total level of artifact: 4. Light source: The artifact can be used as a torch; you can turn on and off the light at will. Cost: 3. Minimum total level of artifact: 4.

Shapeshifting: The artifact can switch between different forms or sizes. Cost: 2. Minimum total level of artifact: 1 per different form + 1 per size change (tiny, light, normal, heavy). Returning: The artifact can be bound to a target as a QD ritual. This target can call it to their hand as a free action. Cost: 2. Minimum total level of artifact: 2 to recall from A, 3 from D range, 4 from same dimension. FOR EACH POINT OF CORRUPTION: Corrupt life: Select the most appropriate of the following: On breaking a target, once per usage per encounter, or on a when using it: take 1 attribute damage. The type of damage is determined on creation, but is often EMP damage. On a count as 2 points of corruption, the others as 1 point of corruption. Magic backlash: Casts a negative spell on the user with no risk for magical mishap. The effect of the spell can be somewhat delayed (usually about 15 minutes). It ignores any magical resistances or immunities. This effect counts

as 1 points of corruption per PL or 0.5 if the effect is delayed. Sow emotions: The item calls for attention. You must fail an insight roll and spend 1 WP to part from it. Others near it will on feeling its power want to steal it on a failed insight roll. This effect counts as 1 point of corruption. Skill reduction: The artifact reduces a skill, even when not actively held. This often come with added effects. Like a skill reduction to animal handling can also make nearby animals uneasy, cause nearby dogs to bark, other animals avoid or attack the user and so on. A skill reduction to sleight of hand, may cause the user to always need to make such a roll when drawing an item, and so forth. Reduce the skills with a [[/r 1d8]] Artifact Die, or whatever Artifact Die the item already has. This effect counts as 1 point of corruption or 2 if it affects multiple skills. GROETMYNDIG (Example Artifact) PL: 3 (1, +2 from corruption) This old sword was made to shout out encouraging words in combat. It was intended as a royal gift, however most uttered sentences are void of intellect, like “Fight on!” and “Hold your hat!”. The shouts are also often made at the most inappropriate times… so the gift was discarded. It grants [[/r 1d8]] artifact item die in combat (1 PL), and will roll a [[/r 1d8]] + its item dice to encourage whenever you or an ally in N range becomes broken in WIT/EMP (ad-hoc 2 PL). A [[/r 1d8]] is added as a negative modifier to all manipulation and stealth rolls for your party, even if sheathed/tucked away, as it often shouts out some generic “You wrong! And you ugly, too!” or other fitting slurs at the worst times (2 points of corruption).

Special: Power Word.

You can teleport yourself a S distance. At PL 2 you can teleport a L distance and at PL 3 you can teleport to a D location. You always need complete line-of-sight to your target destination.

You can take complete control of your victim’s actions. The victim must make an INSIGHT roll with a negative modification equal to the PL. If the roll fails, the victim becomes a puppet without control of his own body. This control only lasts until the victim’s next ordinary turn in the initiative order, and covers one fast and one slow action. The victim cannot perform reactive actions or bonus actions from talents before the PUPPETEER’S actions are performed. The spell has no effect on monsters.

system.ingredient: Piece of ice or a fistful of snow (optional)
system.description: The temperature within the range drops one step per PL. From Summer temperature, to Spring/Fall, to Winter and even colder. If you enter Winter temperatures, the sudden temperature drop will form frost on all surfaces as long as the air is not especially dry. If you further reduce the temperature all non-running water in the area will freeze over a Turn (15 minutes).

Iron weapons scattered on the ground are lifted into the air and circles menacingly around you in a tight formation. For the duration, you gain one bonus point of Armor Rating per PL and anyone ending their round within A from you suffer a melee attack with PL dice, that deals 2 damage, unless it is parried or dodged. You can select the damage type, but it must be one the weapons normally can deal. This spell requires there to be at least one weapon on the ground per PL.

Commanding the element of your choice, you will an elemental servant into being. Its attributes depend on the element used. The elemental will follow your commands but must remain within S distance. Giving orders to your elemental is not an action, but can only be done at your turn. You can dispel it at any time, and it will be dispelled if you are Broken. You can only command one elemental at the same time. You can also use the spell to banish an elemental summoned by another Sorcerer. It then inflicts damage equal to the PL.

ELEMENTAL: An elemental can take many shapes but most of the time they appear humanoid in form. All elementals count as monsters in combat (see page 73 of the Gamemaster’s Guide), but they don’t have monster attacks.

Fire Elemental

STR 2 + PL, AGI 4 + PL

MOVEMENT: 2 (can fly)

SPECIAL: Immune to all non-magical attacks except water. Splashing it with a bucket of water counts as a ranged attack with N range and Weapon Damage 2 (no Gear Bonus).

ATTACKS: Fire Blast (attack with PL+5 Base Dice, N range, Weapon Damage 1, non-typical). Armor offers no protection, and anyone who suffers one point of damage or more catches fire and suffers an additional point of damage until the fire is put out by a successful MOVE roll.

Water Elemental

STR 3 + PL, AGI 3 + PL

MOVEMENT: 2 (swimming), 1 (on land)

SPECIAL: Immune to all non-magical attacks except fire. Hitting it with a burning torch counts as a close combat attack with Weapon Damage 2 (no Gear Bonus).

ATTACKS: Torrent (attack with PL+5 Base Dice, N range, Weapon Damage 1, blunt force). The victim must make a MIGHT roll to stay on their feet. The attack puts out all non-magical fires it hits.

Earth Elemental

STR 5 + PL, AGI 1 + PL

MOVEMENT: 1

ARMOR RATING: 6 + PL

ATTACKS: Fists of stone (close combat attack with PL + 6 Base Dice, Weapon Damage 2).

Wind Elemental

STR 2 + PL, AGI 4 + PL

MOVEMENT: 2 (always flies)

SPECIAL: Immune to all non-magical attacks.

ATTACKS: Whirlwind (attack with PL+3 Base Dice, N range, Weapon Damage 1, affects AGI). The victim must make a MIGHT roll to stay on their feet.

@UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.qB9ID6ywWxrTRlLE]{Chill of the Grave} 1 @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.4FQikVGQXzWtuXgD]{Contaminate} 1 Ghoulish Aura 1 Hand of Doom 2 @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.J20fdqCLWv7squ6x]{Raise the Dead} 2 @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.lCNUWhQuikvwM1L6]{Speak to the Dead} 2 @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.FjsgV8854zSGaVBy]{Steal Life} 3 @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.SNQtKxTwKWfHvjih]{Terror} 3 @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.J0GGS5TLVTUPVLp2]{Weight of Ages} 3 ✥ DURATION: Immediate ✥ INGREDIENT: Severed hand You can claw your way to your victim’s heart magically and squeeze the life from him. This spell inflicts damage to STR equal to the PL. You can extend the range to S if you spend an extra WP (this does not count towards the PL). This spell can only be used against living humanoids.

You can manipulate the levels of fear hormones in the targets blood. This allows the target to ignore the first WIT damage taken due to fear for the duration. Additional PL can either affect more targets or increase the amount of fear damage that each target can ignore.

Skilled Sorcerers and Druids can BIND spells to dead objects to create magical traps or powerful magical artifacts. You cast the spell like any other and choose how many WP to spend, but you must also spend extra WP to bind your spell to an object instead of unleashing its power immediately. Rituals cannot be BOUND. Roll for any overcharge and mishap when the spell is BOUND. The extra WP do affect this roll, but don’t count toward the PL. If you spend 1 additional WP, the magic lingers for one day, or until the spell is triggered. If you spend 2 additional WP, the magic lingers forever, but dissipates when the spell is triggered. Spending 5 additional WP binds the spell to the chosen object forever, and it can be triggered once per day. You can bind the spell in whatever manner you wish. You decide how the spell is triggered. Common methods include a certain phrase being uttered or that the object is opened, broken or thrown to the ground. Once the spell has triggered, it works just like it would if it had been cast normally.

system.ingredient: Piece of ice or a fistful of snow (optional)
system.description: You summon a cloud of icicles and hurl it at a target within S distance. The attack inflicts damage equal to the PL (stab wound), and the target becomes COLD.
You summon a bright light that dispels all shadows within N range, i.e., in the same Zone as you.

You can make a fistsized chunk of volcanic rock explode in a cascade of magma that burns anyone standing too close and sets fire to combustible objects. The stone can explode in the desired location with a successful MARKSMANSHIP roll; otherwise the explosion takes place within N range of the location in question. Alternatively, you can make a suitable stone on the ground explode in a magma cascade just as the target walks by, without making a skill roll. Everyone within A range of the explosion suffers one point of damage to STR per PL.

You can then enter the dreams of anyone you have encountered, as long as they too are sleeping. They are allowed to make an insight roll with a negative modification equal to the PL to shake you out if they want to. During the dream you can discern their location in the world. You may also communicate to the recipient, but they can choose to ignore you if they do not want this. You can also turn the dream into a nightmare; this makes the target unable to benefit from sleep during that QD. If done over a period of days equaling the targets WIT, they are likely to go insane, if so, you can roll on the horror injury table, to see the effect.

system.ingredient: Piece of ice or a fistful of snow (optional)
system.description: You, for just a fraction of a second, radiate immense cold in an explosion like manner around you. All subjects within the range suffer 1 point of STR and AGI damage from becoming cold. They also become frozen stuck to the ground. They must make a might roll, before they intend to use a move skill or take actions that will move them, if they fail the might roll, their intended action also fails, they lose that action and will stay stuck to the ground until they can succeed a new might roll during future actions. If the might roll succeed, they are no longer stuck to the ground. Monsters are immune to these effects. All zones with the range also become rough terrain, as everything within becomes coated in a thin layer of ice. Increase the range to L at PL 2.
The target negates the next damage to attributes they receive, up to the PL. If this negates damage from pushed, they also do not yield any WP. You may optionally spend PL to add additional targets.

You can perfectly sense the magnetic fields of the land and build an internal map using it. Gain a +1 bonus per PL to survival when you survey the lands, lead the way or in otherwise navigate, like a maze or so for the rest of the session.

system.ingredient: See Epic Magic (Epic Magic ingredients do not increase Power Level)
system.description:
Special: Epic Magic.

This is an Epic Spell, see the description for those in this booklet. Each PL requires an ingredient. It allows you to channel nature’s forces to bring back someone from the dead– not as undead, but truly alive. You don’t even need the body of the target; the spell can recreate it, removing any permanent physical injuries as you see fit, also removing what is left of any corpse out there in the world. It cannot reverse age, or a shattered elven ruby, but can create a new body for an intact ruby. The more time that has passed since the target died, the more difficult it is to convince it to return. For each week that has passed since the target died, the spell requires an additional PL. A target that doesn’t know you well, might also need to be convinced to return with a successful manipulation roll. You can however only send your thoughts and intents to the target, not receive any answers back. The spell will on resurrection irreversibly erase any memories of life beyond the veil.

system.ingredient: An insect that you crush to its death
system.description:
Special: Power Word.

A broken creature within A is immediately killed as if you performed a coup de grace. You do not suffer from any negative effects if you aren’t cold blooded. Each added PL increases the spells range.

system.ingredient: Blanket of insects (optional; consumed if available)
system.description: You are able to launch large bee stingers from your body. You gain the ability to as a fast action, make a ranged attack, within S range that rolls your marksmanship, a [[/r 1d10]] Artifact Die and 1 Item Die per PL. Weapon Damage 1, stab wound. This spell does NOT create any blanket of insects.

You can trace a person carrying iron items up to one day after the person passed by, since the weak magnetism of the metal affects the ground where the individual has walked. Each item leaves a unique trace. The trace cannot be followed in water.

You can restore permanently lost attribute points. To restore an attribute lost to create an artifact, you must as an ingredient destroy an artifact of at least equal power. You can also restore an attribute lost to age, but it is then sadly only restored for a week. You can also restore an attribute lost from other events, like through death. The spell only needs a PL of 1, but each restoration on a subject double the required PL to restore it a new.
This spell can guide you to the right path when you face a difficult decision. Once you have cast the spell, the GM must tell you which decision or choice she believes is the wisest.

You throw away a held melee weapon containing iron towards an opponent. It counts as a ranged x hit dealing 2 damage. The target is allowed to parry or dodge the attack as if it were a melee attack. Armor rating can also protect against the damage. An extra PL can be used to have the weapon return to your hand. PL can also be spent to add extra hit x, or to add targets the attack bounces to (and is repeated against).

This ritual takes a QD and requires a willing subject. The target is restored 1 year of youth for every PL. However, the target also loses any experience, skills and talents accumulated over these years. They will retain some memories from this period of time, but the memories will grow weaker and it will be almost impossible for the subject to tell exactly when they happened. If the target has been subjected to the @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.J0GGS5TLVTUPVLp2]{Weight of Ages} spell, the spell will counter these years first, without any negative side effects.

This spell animates machine-like objects, granting them the ability to perform actions when manipulated. The object gains STR 1, with a +2 bonus per extra PL. It operates for a QD, but PL could also be used to double the duration. So, it could power a pump, power a mill, or power a mechanical spider and make it steerable. Crafting the machine requires metal, a forge, and successful rolls. If made into an artifact, a good complication could be that it would require fuel in order to operate.

system.ingredient: Blanket of insects (optional; consumed if available)
system.description: Your swarm turns into edible pupae, mealworms, etc. The spell creates one unit of mealworms per PL. You can either cook mealworms into food just like if they were meat, or treat them as food just as they are. Anyone that eats them will then however take 1 EMP damage, unless they know Swarm Magic. The shelf-life of mealworms is 1 week, and even longer if they are stored in a root cellar, just like with regular food. This spell does NOT create any blanket of insects.

You raise the elements to form a wall in the targeted area. Any creatures standing in its way, may choose which side to stand on, but they will fall prone unless they succeed a move roll with a penalty equal to the PL. Monsters do not fall prone. The walls will occupy a space up to 3 meters heigh and up to 10 meters long, and can be slightly curved, but no sharp corners. PL can be used to empower the wall, se descriptions below, or they can be used to double a dimension of the wall, so with 4 extra PL, you can encircle yourself within a 25-meter radius wall. When the spell ends the wall crumbles away and only traces of it will remain. Earth: Can take 2 STR damage +2 per PL damage, with a natural armor rating of 8. Fire: Deal 2 dice per PL fire damage to anyone that crosses it. Anyone that takes damage also catches fire. Water: All attacks through it, suffers a penalty equal to the PL. Passing though it counts as rough terrain with a -1 penalty to the move roll per PL. Wind: All ranged attacks from one side of the wall, specified upon casting it, suffers a penalty equal to the PL. Passing though it counts as rough terrain with a -1 penalty to the move roll per PL.

system.ingredient: Blood (required – does not count towards the total Power Level)
system.description: You smear blood over your hand, and can from that form a hand print of blood floating in the air. This hand print can then fly away and be directed at a distance. It takes your full attention to control it, and it can only perform very basic actions like: open a door, pick something up, or pull a lever. The hand print vanishes if you move it outside the range. It lasts one round per PL and can carry an item taking up a maximum of 1 weight slot per PL. If you need it to temporarily pull something heavy, it has a might level of 0 and a STR of 1 per PL. It will leave marks of blood on everything it touches.

system.ingredient: Piece of ice or a fistful of snow (optional)
system.description: You become immune to all effects of cold. For each additional PL, you can increase the duration a QD or extend the effect to another person within N range.

system.ingredient: A mirror or polished piece of metal
system.description: This spell works just like @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.q7pUflnmCYLf1BtH]{Fata Morgana}, except that you only get to roll for insight if someone interacts with the illusion. On a failure it still tries to fool all your senses. Some interactions will be too hard to emulate correctly, for instance: You could during the first second think that you are standing on an illusionary bridge, but would start to question what happened when you suddenly lay bleeding on the ground below, without remembering falling. You could also think and feel like if you were on fire, but you would in reality find yourself unharmed when the effect ends.

Wherever you go, the land around you absorbs your tracks and masks your scent. It also reduces sounds from sneaking and therefor grants a +2 modifier to stealth rolls, as long as you are outdoors. Affects one ally per PL.

You make a rock shoot up under the feet of a target, making them stand on a pillar. They must succeed a move roll or fall prone. The pillar is 3 meters high per PL. If the target hits a ceiling, it takes 1 damage per PL. Armor will not reduce this damage. A target wanting to get down can either choose to jump or climb. A normal humanoid can climb this pillar at a rate of 3 meters per successful move roll, each such roll uses a fast action. Any created pillars are unstable and falls over or crumbles after your next round. Large targets will only be moved 1 meter per PL.

system.ingredient: Piece of ice or a fistful of snow (optional)
system.description: The spell summons a sword of ice that functions like a normal shortsword with a [[/r 1d8]] Artifact Die. By increasing the PL by one, you can summon a longsword, and by two, a two-handed sword. Alternatively, increasing the PL by one can upgrade the Artifact Die to [[/r 1d10]].

system.ingredient: Blanket of insects (optional; consumed if available)
system.description: During the duration, if there is any blanket of insects available, it will grant you blindsight, allowing you to ignore darkness up to S range. Any blanket of insects will now also follow you when you move. The spell lasts a QD per PL, and during this time you also gain a bonus to scouting equaling the PL, as long as there are insects near whatever you could notice with the roll. This spell creates a blanket of insects upon casting it.

Special: Power Word; REACTION; Reactive.

You have mastered magnetic energies enough, so that you are even able to repel and redirect magical energies. When you detect a magical spell cast within or through N range of you, then you can cast this spell as a fast reaction. If so is done, the original spells PL will be lowered with this spells PL, and you can rebound, at least a part of the original spell, as if cast anew with reverse spell’s PL, and redirect it towards any targets. You can even choose who should count as the caster of the rebound spell. This also means that if reverse spell’s PL beats the original spell, then the PL of the rebound spell, will be even higher than that of the original spell. The rebound spell will not roll any magical dice or cause any magical mishaps itself, but both the original spell and the reverse spell can.

You plant thoughts in your targets head. Unless the target succeeds a insight roll with a penalty equal to this spells PL, you can rewrite their personality and very thoughts, but unless you obscured the magic at least others would know you cast a spell on them. Your ability to rewrite their mind lingers for as long as you both remain within S range. But any rewrite you have done will remain permanently. Monsters are immune to this spell.

Forcing any nearby source of water or snow to do your bidding, you unleash a flood wave or small avalanche against your victims. The targets suffer a total amount of damage equal to the PL – you can distribute the damage as you see fit. All victims who take damage are thrown to the ground, and, if you use snow, they also become COLD.

system.ingredient: Blanket of insects (optional; consumed if available)
system.description: After the ritual, you can gain the ability to release or absorb a blanket of insects as a slow action. The duration is permanent, but ends if you ever become Broken.

As long as there are living plants in your current hex, you can lend their powers. The spell causes all plants in the hex to sprout and blossom. When the ritual ends gain twice the PL in WP. The spell cannot be cast again in the same map hex for a month.

Special: Cast with another spell.

If you want to cast a spell unnoticed, you must OBSCURE your magic. This requires 1 extra WP that does not count toward the PL of the spell. OBSCURING magic does not count as an action in itself. To detect your OBSCURED spell, another magic user must actively survey the area by casting @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.kZPxv7HeAMouHPnE]{Sense Magic}.

Your voice doesn’t only affect stone, but also metals that have been mined from the mountain. This ritual allows you to create weapons and other items of metal, but also, for example, to bend prison bars and open shackles. You can create all metal weapons from the weapons tables (see Chapter 5) with a Gear Bonus equal to the PL, up to a maximum of +3. The weapon’s other stats are according to the weapons table. When you use IRON SONG, you must have access to the right raw materials, as if you are using CRAFTING to create an object.

system.duration: Travel after a Quarter Day's sleep
system.description: In your sleep, you can travel to any previously visited location. You bring with you any items on your person, but no animals or bulky baggage. Each additional PL allows you to bring another sleeping creature with you on your journey, but only to places that you have personally visited. You are transported after a QD’s sleep and wake up fully rested at your destination.

As long as you are on solid ground not made out of sandstone, limestone or marble, a geyser can sprout forth from under a target. The target takes 1 point of damage from the heat per PL and each PL also counts as a shove x towards tripping the target. Anyone within A of the target suffer a 2 dice attack per PL, each rolled x both deals damage and counts as a shove as per above.

system.ingredient: An insanity of your own (not consumed)
system.description: The victim must make an insight roll with a negative modification equal to the PL. If the roll fails, the symbol makes the victim go partially insane for a week. Come up with an insanity or pick one from the critical horror injury, except for catatonic or heart attack. Each added PL also doubles the duration. The spell has no effect on monsters.

You can meld your mind with that of a hawk and gain its inhuman sight. You can see the details of anything within D range, everything from horizon to horizon. You see all details and can identify specific people.

Your song can shape stone according to your will. This spell lets you create a wall, build a bridge, or raise a staircase from the ground. You can only create crude constructions. PL 1 will summon a construction in the same Zone as you. Every PL beyond that allows you to create something that stretches into one more neighboring Zone. For example, PL 4 lets you summon a construction reaching across four Zones.
You increase your WIT with the PL for a QD.

system.ingredient: Piece of ice or a fistful of snow (optional)
system.description: Target must succeed a might roll with a penalty equal to the spell level, or they will become cold and completely incased in ice. The ice can be broken if dealt 5 points of damage, until then the target is rendered unconscious and without the need to breathe. While the spell is in effect, all ongoing physical effects, like from poison or bleeding, are also temporarily halted. Lasts 1 turn per PL.

system.ingredient: Piece of ice or a fistful of snow (optional)
system.description: Everyone within a L range, must seek cover or risk being pelted by oversized hail. The hail counts as ranged attacks that targets everyone in the open each round. Roll the attacks with a single [[/r 1d6]] die per PL. The attacks deal 1 blunt damage per rolled x. The spell is centered on you, and moves with you. It can be made to exclude a N range around yourself as a safe area.

You can ask a short “yes” or “no” question about anything in the world. The GM must answer “yes,” “no,” or “maybe.” She cannot lie. The GM can choose “maybe” even if she knows the answer, but believes that the true answer may disrupt the game. Note that true or false is not an objective fact, but is defined by who is asking the question. This person’s morals and beliefs can make something that is true for her false for someone else.

A staff, club or heavy club grows forth with a Gear Bonus equal to the PL, up to a maximum of +3. The weapon’s other stats are according to the weapon’s table. After a QD, the weapons gear bonus is reduced to that of a regular staff, club or heavy club. If grown from any special tree with wood that can grant higher than normal weapon bonuses (if any such modules are used), then such extra bonuses can be permanently retained.

system.ingredient: See Epic Magic (Epic Magic ingredients do not increase Power Level)
system.description:
Special: EPIC SPELL; Epic Magic.

This is an Epic Spell, see the description for those in this booklet. Each PL requires an ingredient. This ritual can be used to make a permanent underground stronghold within a mountain hex. Zone: You create a large open zone that can house buildings. It will be made stable and have a normal temperature, despite if there are any nearby lava, and will protect it from natural events, like lava, earthquakes and so on. Cost 1 per area of space that can fit up to 2000 stone or 1000 wood of buildings. Lava moat: Lava provides a moat for the location, and adds an extra defense rating. It also provides illumination and works like a fireplace for the stronghold. Cost 1. Raise buildings: Stone buildings in your zones are partially preconstructed. You will need to succeed craft rolls during this ritual to have them operational at once, but if you fail, you will at least still have their raw materials in stone. Gain buildings for up to 2000 stone per zone. Cost: 2. Earthquakes: Roll a [[/r 1d6]] each week, on a a person in the stronghold is injured and a random function in the stronghold partially breaks. The function can be repaired on a successful crafting roll and a QD of work. The person is broken and suffers a critical injury rolled on the blunt force table. Can be taken as 1 point of corruption. Foul smoke: The area is filled with bad smelling gas. A chosen attribute will not heal naturally while in the area. Can be taken as 1 point of corruption. Infested: The area has attracted demons or some other pest. Roll for weekly stronghold events twice, if the second result is higher, and it can be caused by the pest, take it. Can be taken as 2 points of corruption.

system.ingredient: Same as for the confusion spell
system.description: Target up to one plus PL persons within the range. The victims then must make an insight roll to resist the spell, or be affected just as the @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.WR1vyeaL0PeSjRJ9]{Confusion} spell.

Up to one target per PL only needs a one turn (15 minute) power nap, to have it counts as the required sleep for the day, or to remove the sleepless condition. This sleep does not count as rest and cannot be used to, at the same time, perform any other oneiromancy magic. This spell is considered heretic by most oneiromancers. It is only taught by renegade daydreamers.

For the duration of the spell, you become immune to all forms of fire, including dragon fire and lava. For each PL another person in your vicinity can become fire’s friend too. However, the spell does not protect equipment or clothes.

Special: Power Word.

You can teleport away an object you touch to a random location within your current world map, quickly disposing evidence or even as a way of escaping yourself. At PL 1, you can teleport away 1 light object, at PL 2, you can teleport away multiple heavy objects, and at PL 3 you can teleport away a humanoid you touch. An unwilling subject can try to resist being sucked away. This then requires them to succeed a might roll.
As long as the ground where you stand can support plant life, it will after the duration spring to full life, immediately delivering 1 unit of vegetables per PL.

You animate the undergrowth in a large outdoors area, turning the ground into rough terrain for your enemies, and if it was rough terrain, you can treat it as open for your allies. Your enemies have to roll move when they run into such a zone. Failure means they managed to get into the zone, but fall down. The effect lasts for 1 round per PL. Added PL can also give the vines thorns, causing any failed roll to roll against a paralyzing poison with a potency of 3 per such added PL.

You and each subject within N range when the spell was cast will be blessed by nature. Each QD they spend doing activities outdoors, outside of settlements, will also count as rest. Each additional PL adds a day to the duration.
You can make yourself completely immune to heat and cold (see page 111). You take no damage from fire.
You can meld your mind with the spirit of the cat, and move without a sound. You can cast this spell instead of rolling SNEAK, and you will succeed automatically. Each PL counts as one x.

Up to one willing target per PL falls into a coma like sleep for one QD. During this time, they are free to spend days in a dreamworld. They may spend any amount of time here, resting, sleeping, training, healing physical and mental injuries, that also will heal in the real world. The target may exit the dream palace at any time atwill on their own. The only downside is that all time spent here, will accelerate their aging. A year spent here will age you as if you spent a year of your life in the real world too. The dreams can be even further accelerated by added PL. Add +1 PL to have the comalike state only take up a turn, and +2 PL to have it only take up a round of the targets’ actions. They still slump down to the floor though, counting as both prone and disarmed when the spell ends. Dream palace should not be used more than once per day, or the participants might have to make an insight roll to not want to stay in it “forever”, killing their body in the real world over the selected duration through old age.

You grant yourself or a creature you touch the ability to breath water as if it was air, eliminating the danger of drowning. Each PL increases the number of creatures you can affect by one or increases the duration by one turn. These extra effects can be combined.
You increase your EMP with the PL for a QD.
Controlling the element of water, you draw the fluids out of a living victim. They immediately become THIRSTY and suffer damage to AGI equal to the PL. Armor has no effect.

As long as you successfully observe the use of magic over a maximum of a S distance, you can on your following round copy the magical signature of that spell, as long as the PL of your Copy Magic equals the rank of the spell. When you cast the spell, the GM will tell you the minimum PL you need. You can at this time abort the spell, but it will then still cost you your action. You gain knowledge of the spell for a week. During this time, you may cast this spell as if you had a its corresponding magical discipline one rank below that of the spell, but down to a minimum rank of 1, if you are not already higher. If you want to spend XP to learn the spell’s discipline during this time, it will count as a teacher of a rank one less than that of the spell, but to a minimum rank of 1. If you ever fulfill all criteria’s for permanently knowing the spell, during its duration, you can choose to learn it permanently. Copy Magic cannot be used to copy monster abilities, even if they are spell like.

A normal sized door you touch opens as if you had succeeded a might roll to push it open or a sleight of hand roll to pick its lock. Either way, the action is very noisy and not very delicate, triggering any traps. If a door cannot be picked or would apply a penalty to a might roll, you must add one PL for each negative modifier. Each added PL can also counter one level of the @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.lwxYJkoSNiKnhRYh]{Reinforce} spell.

You can affect the sleep of one or multiple living creatures by injecting nightmares into their minds. The victims suffer damage to WIT equal to the PL. A victim that has its WIT reduced to zero suffers a critical fear injury. For every two additional PL another victim is affected. The nightmares also render the creature SLEEPLESS for the next day. The spell has no effect on monsters.

As long as there is lava around, you can absorb some of its power. Gain a number of WP equal to twice the PL. While performing the ritual, you are completely immune to fire damage and when you are done, any existing lava within L range will harden and cool. If this cools a more or less permanent lava flow, the effect only lasts for a QD.

You permanently end all magical effects with a duration other than immediate inside the range. Must be cast with a PL equal or greater than that of the ongoing effects, or it simply fails to affect that magic. It will affect object with bound magic (see the @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.Yw1R9hqQJuUx2Ktr]{Bind Magic} spell), but it will not affect artifacts, unless you present a material cost at least equal to what would be needed to create it.

You can use this spell to steal WP from others or to give your WP to someone else. The base cost to cast the spell is 1 WP, and you can then take or give as many WP as you want. If your target opposes the TRANSFER, it is not so easy – in this case, you can transfer no more WP than the PL of the TRANSFER. The WP used to cast TRANSFER are spent and are not transferred.

By calling forth the element of fire in the heart of another living being, you cause your victim to be overcome by anger and rage. Make an opposed roll with a number of Base Dice equal to twice the PL against the INSIGHT skill of the victim. You cannot push the roll. If you win, the victim goes berserk and must immediately attack everyone in N range and keep fighting until they are Broken, or all enemies have fled or are Broken. No effect against monsters or creatures that lack WIT.

You can temporarily reverse the gravity of a metal object you touch, caused by a repelling magnetic force between it and the ground. A target carrying metal armor can be made to fly using the spell. If you target yourself, you can fly during the duration. Any other target may try to avoid it by fending of your touch with a dodge or parry. An affected target can be moved/flied with your actions, a target may try to negate this if there is anything to hold on to with a might roll. Each PL adds one round to the duration. Targets are unlikely to be able to move on their own and will fall to the ground when the duration ends.

You can enhance your vision to be unnaturally sharp, and see details at D range as if you stood right next to the object in question. TRUE SIGHT also lets you see in darkness, through smoke and fog, and automatically see through any kind of disguise or shapeshift. You must have a clear line of sight to whatever you want to look at.

system.ingredient: Piece of ice or a fistful of snow (optional)
system.description: A wall of ice grows up from the ground in the targeted area. Any creatures standing in its way, may choose which side to stand on, but they will fall prone unless they succeed a move roll with a penalty equal to the PL. Monsters do not fall prone. The walls will occupy a space 3 meters heigh and 10 meters long, and can be slightly curved, but no sharp corners. Any section of the ice will break enough so that the one breaking it can step through, if it takes 2 damage per PL with an armor rating of 5. PL can also be used to double a dimension of the wall, so with 4 extra PL, you can encircle yourself within a 25-meter radius wall of ice. While the effect of the wall is permanent, the wall will take damage from warmer temperatures. Extreme temperature: 1/minute, summer temperature: 1/turn, spring/autumn temperature: 1/QD.

This can be cast as a ritual or as a spell. As a ritual: Designate up to one target per PL that participates in the ritual when you cast this spell to become your blood vessels. The targets need not be there willingly. As a spell: Gain a number of WP equal to twice the PL as long as one of your blood vessels are in the same hex on the map as you. This deals damage to the vessel equal to the PL (slash wound). Each vessel can be used a maximum of once per day.

As a sorcerer or druid, you automatically sense whenever someone uses magic within S range or if an item you hold is charged with magical power. If you want to know more about what kind of magic is involved, you must cast the SENSE MAGIC spell. Using this spell is also required to detect OBSCURED magic (see below) – your PL must then be equal to or higher than the PL of the @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.eVxabvHNIrLXpuaX]{Obscure Magic} spell.

You can bend animals, both wild and tame, to your will. The animal can, for example, break off an attack, track down an enemy, run to where you want it to and deliver a message, allow you to ride on it, or even attack your op- ponents. You cannot control an animal with a STR higher than twice the PL. The PL must be one step higher if the animal is agitated, scared or in combat. If you force an animal to act in a way that is outside its normal behavior – like make it perform tricks, for example – the PL needs to be one step higher. You can only control one animal at a time. This spell cannot be used against monsters.

While in an adventure site, this spell will give you a perfect sense of a mountain’s hills, tunnels and caves, allowing you to ask for directions from one spot to another. Giving you descriptions of nearby areas and allowing you to take the shortest or most optimal route. It will not give information on any creatures or objects inside, but larger structures like stronghold functions can be sensed. While outside of an adventure site, during journey travels: Then while travelling through a passible mountain range, the spell will almost make it feel like new hidden paths opens up for you and your adventurers, allowing you to travel the mountain at 3 hexes per QD. No one else will find these paths, as if they never where there. Lasts for 1 QD per PL.

system.ingredient: See Epic Magic (Epic Magic ingredients do not increase Power Level)
system.description:
Special: EPIC SPELL; Epic Magic.

This is an Epic Spell, see the description for those in this booklet. Each PL requires an ingredient. This ritual can be used to a permanently alter time within a location or move a location through time and space. Quicken time: A QD spent here only takes 3h in the “real” world. This is can be good for crafting, sleeping and many other things. Hirelings require increased salaries and use more food from this though. Cost 3 for a stronghold location or similar sized building. Cost +1 for each extra stronghold locations or similar sized building. Slow time: A QD spent here takes two QD in the “real” world. This is can be good for a root cellar, as it keeps goods fresh for longer. Cost 2 for a stronghold location or similar sized building. Cost +1 for each extra 2 stronghold locations or similar sized buildings. Through time and space: The location can be shifted forward in time and change location to another hex on the map. Cost 2 for up to 5 locations or similarly sized buildings, each added PL doubles the amount of locations or buildings affected. Transport stronghold up to 10 hexes. Added PL can each double this. The transport is instant. Unpredictable: A slowed or quickened area roll a [[/r 1d6]], after a complete usage of the area, on a the opposite time effect happened instead. A “through time and space” effect fumbles one of the following things, roll a [[/r 1d6]]. 1-2: A function and its occupants was left behind or appeared somewhere else. 3-4: You appear [[/r 1d6]] hexes of your intended location. 5-6: You appear [[/r 1d3]] months later in time than intended. Count as 1 point of corruption.

system.ingredient: Body part from a dead person
system.description: You can speak with the dead. You must be within N range of where the victim died or lies buried. You must know the victim’s name. You can speak with the dead for a few minutes and ask a few simple questions. The GM decides what the dead can and will answer – the dead aren’t always cooperative! If the victim’s remains are reasonably intact you can speak directly with the corpse, otherwise you hear the dead as a disembodied ghost voice in your head. This spell cannot be used against undead.

You can read and fully understand everything regarding a single magical artifact or magical effect, just as if you would have been a god reading through the rules of the universe. If it is used on a magical spell that you saw in action during the past turn, or one you can read about in a grimoire, or similar, it can give you a rune of that spell per PL. Such runes can be used by you, to (once per rune) be able to recast the spell as if they were from the Symbolism discipline. These runes themselves does not store any PL, so you decide upon using them how many WP you want to spend on it. These runes also do not count towards the spell’s ingredients; so see the spells original description for those.

system.ingredient: Blanket of insects (optional; consumed if available)
system.description: You, your blanket of insects and all other insect effects created by your Swarm magic become resistant to a chosen element per PL for the duration of the spell, or until it is cast anew. Elements that can be chosen are fire, cold, lightning or acid. This resistance reduces any damage taken from the element by half, round down, and removes any previous weaknesses against the element. This spell creates a blanket of insects when it is cast.

system.ingredient: Piece of ice or a fistful of snow (optional)
system.description: You exhale an ice cold cloud of snow against a target within N range. The victim must immediately win an opposed roll of MIGHT against twice the PL (the roll is not an action) or be frozen in place for a 15 minute turn. If the roll fails, the victim cannot move at all and becomes COLD.

system.duration: Takes effect in one turn; sleep lasts a Quarter Day
system.description: @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.qTqlMbw92gnMy07I]{Sleep} lasts a QD unless the sleeper is woken up. You sing a quiet lullaby that makes humanoid creatures within range fall into a deep slumber unless they succeed with an INSIGHT roll (not an action) with a negative modification equal to the PL. The sleepers can be woken up, but will stay asleep if left alone. The lullaby also affects allies unless they somehow plug their ears.

You reinforce a wall or door with the toughness of the earth. A door cannot longer be opened or picked during the duration, and the targeted object doubles its armor rating. The effect lasts for a turn at PL 1. At PL 2 it lasts for a QD and at PL 3 it lasts for a week.

Using this spell, you protect a person (no bigger than a human) or a location (no bigger than a human) from magic. The PL of any spells cast against that person or place during the QD is decreased by the PL of the MAGICAL SEAL.

system.ingredient: Piece of ice or a fistful of snow (optional)
system.description: A cold target must succeed an endurance roll with a penalty equal to the PL or become your thrall, following your commands just as if they were a mindless undead. It matters not if they are human, undead or so on. This spell will immediately end if a thrall comes into contact with fire or loses the cold condition.

Special: Power Word.

A target carrying an item out of iron is subjected to a disarm attempt with one x per PL. Any extra x than what was needed can be used to fling the weapon away a zone from A to N, S, L or D range. If a item is flung, it can also be used to try to hit someone, roll marksmanship, it has a base damage of 1 per zone it could have been flung, but will then land near that target on a miss or within arm’s reach on a hit.

system.ingredient: Blanket of insects (optional; consumed if available)
system.description:
After 1 turn (15 minutes), insects will have completely devoured any bodies, and all traces of blood and gore within the area of the spell. As long as there were remains to consume, the insects gain enough energy to restore you of 1

point of STR and AGI damage per PL when the spell ends. This spell creates a blanket of insects when it ends.

system.ingredient: Piece of ice or a fistful of snow (optional)
system.description: You turn your victim’s heart to ice. The victim suffers one point of damage to WIT per PL and becomes COLD. Armor has no effect.

You can turn an object to stone. Leather can in this way be turned to stone leather and ancient wood can in this way be turned into stone wood. Dwarves often use the latter for making for very strong and age resistant bearings in their most important mines. If used on a living subject it deals 1 AGI damage per PL, resisted with an insight roll. A person dropping to zero AGI from this is permanently turned into stone. Monsters are immune.

You become incorporeal with the ability to fly at a movement rate of 1. During this time, you can move through walls and other solid objects. You cannot affect anything physically while the spell lasts and you are immune to physical damage, but you can use and be affected by spells. Fire can also damage you. You may end the spell at will. If the spell ends while you are inside a solid object, you die. If you die while the spell is active, you are forever stuck in the form of a more or less mindless ghost. It lasts for 1 round per PL.

You are so in tune with the forces of nature that you can summon a drastic weather shift in the map hexagon where you are. A smaller shift, from cloudy to rain or from dead calm to a light breeze, requires PL 1. Unusual weather phenomena that still stay within what is apt for the season – a snowstorm in winter, blazing heat in the summer, or hard winds and lashing rains in the fall – require PL 2. To summon completely unnatural weather, such as a snowstorm in the summer or a heatwave in the middle of winter, requires PL 3.

system.ingredient: An hourglass (item is not consumed if you borrow Willpower Points)
system.description:
Special: Power Word.

You ask your possible future selves to lend you some power backwards in time. Gain 2 WP for every PL. You must then in the future cast the spell again without gaining WP to send power back to your past self. You cannot cast the spell again until the full dept in PL has been paid.

You can cast this spell to bind yourself to a place you have a deep connection to, like your stronghold, or a place where anyone you strongly care about lives. This requires you to inscribe any such area with a recall symbol. You can be bound to multiple places, as long as you have a strong emotional connection to each one. You can later recast this spell to be transport yourself to one of your recall points, as long as the inscribed recall symbol remains. You may transport one additional person per PL.

system.ingredient: Meat from an animal stronger than you
system.description: You increase your STR with the PL for a QD.

system.ingredient: Blanket of insects (optional; consumed if available)
system.description: Create one swarm of fireflies per PL. They can once per round, during your round, be directed to any point within the range and will then dimly light up anything within N range of that location. Seeing into such zones no longer counts as being in total darkness (see Player’s handbook page 112). One swarm of fireflies is lost per turn, turning into a blanket of insects. Any one swarm of fireflies can at any-time, during your round, be dismissed to create a blanket of insects.

An intense ancient fire fills the target, making them glow from within. The target regains PL points in all attributes, gains PL WP, ignores attribute damage when calculating how many dice to roll, reduces all kinds of further damage taken by half (rounded down), and draws an extra initiative card, acting twice per round. It lasts for one turn per PL, and when the duration ends the target’s insides are unavoidably burned up, and it slumps down dead. No amount of fire resistances can help against this fate. A target that takes almost no defensive or hostile actions during the duration of the spell, instead just trying to concentrate on remaining calm, can at the end try to make an insight roll to avoid the spells grim fate. They roll with a -1 penalty per defensive or hostile action taken during the duration.
You can bend your body passing into small spaces just as if you were half of your regular height and width. Each added PL doubles the duration.
You can strike your enemy with the force of a great bear. You hit automatically and cause damage equal to the PL. The attack cannot be PARRIED or DODGED, but armor has normal effect.
As long as you are in a hex mostly filled with green vegetation, you can roll for make camp without it taking a QD. The roll gains a +2 bonus per extra PL.

system.ingredient: Parchment where the spell is inscribed
system.description:
Special: Cast with another spell.

Cast together with another spell, that is not a ritual. That spell now targets a zone. If it had a duration, it now targets everyone within the new area as long as they stay within. If a target leaves the zone, any effects bestowed upon them by the spell, immediately ends. If it was an immediate effect, is now cast up to once per turn to the first one entering the zone. Any positive effects the spell had will be reverted when you leave the zone, while any detrimental effects will stay. The spell can no longer differentiate friends from foes, but the original spellcaster may render the spell inactive at will when entering within N range. You can increase the zone size to S or L for 1 to 2 additional PL, respectively. You may mold the target area somewhat, like “only target the city walls”. It normally lasts for a week, but you can increase the duration to a month or a year for 2 to 4 additional PL, respectively. Regardless of this a living spell will also begin to fade out upon the spellcasters death. Living spells are by nature very unpredictable, so the GM is allowed to tweak and alter the spell somewhat.

This spell concentrates the energy of the sorcerer’s own blood. You gain a number of WP equal to twice the PL. The effect is temporary, however. Your newly won WP must be used in the next round, or they are lost. If you use a living sacrifice as an ingredient for your spell, it must be sacrificed before you cast the spell. A small animal is enough.

You can charge a symbol with power. The symbol must be drawn on or carved into an object, which is then charged with a number of WP equal to the PL. You can use the symbol later to cast spells, emptying its stored WP. You don’t need to @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.Yw1R9hqQJuUx2Ktr]{Bind Magic} to use this spell. Other spellbinders skilled in the art of runes can use your POWER RUNES if they can access them, so keep them to yourself!

system.ingredient: Blanket of insects (optional; consumed if available)
system.description: You and up to one party member per added PL will not be attacked by insects for the duration, unless you attack or provoke them first. Monstrous insects or Queens can see through the pheromones, but this spell allows you to use animal handling to avoid having them see you as a threat. If one insect attacks you, it can break the effect on others. This spell can have limited effects on humanoids too, it grants a +1 bonus to manipulation per PL for the duration, but a pro tip is to, at the same time, just maybe avoid having insects crawling all around? This spell does NOT create any blanket of insects.

system.ingredient: Piece of ice or a fistful of snow (optional)
system.description: You create a shield of ice that works as a normal small shield with a [[/r 1d8]] Artifact Die. If you increase the PL by one, you can create a large shield or upgrade the Artifact Die to [[/r 1d10]]. The shield may only be used by you.

Commanding the element of wind, you suffocate a victim by literally pulling the air out of their lungs. The target suffers one point of damage at the start of each subsequent round, for a number of rounds equal to the PL. Armor has no effect. If the victim is Broken by the effect of the spell, they die after [[/r 1d6]] rounds unless saved with a HEAL roll. While under the effect of the spell, the victim cannot talk or scream.

You call animals within the map hex to your location and you may specify what types of animals that should heed your call. The nearest animals within the hex, with a combined STR no higher that 4x PL will answer your call. They are called from within your current Hex and it usually takes a turn (15 minutes) for them to arrive, but this could be shorter if they are nearby. You gain no control of them after they arrive.

system.ingredient: See Epic Magic (Epic Magic ingredients do not increase Power Level)
system.description:
Special: EPIC SPELL; Epic Magic.

This is an Epic Spell, see the description for those in this booklet. Each PL requires an ingredient. This ritual can be used to a permanently give a magnetic effect to an area. @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.777fikAIqqYkE7vz]{Fixate}: Works like the @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.777fikAIqqYkE7vz]{Fixate} spell, but becomes permanent. You may either fixate up to a heavy object for 1 PL, or fixate a something as large and heavy as a wagon for 2, a house for 3, or an entire settlement for 4. As these objects might not be of iron, you can instead have the spell @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.EjdIrJkb01836q48]{Magnetize} the ground they stand on and fixate that instead, this costs no extra PL. During the ritual, you can move the fixated object anywhere within-the rituals lineof-sight. Controlled: You can have the one in use of an object be able to control a fixated object. Either being allowed to move it at a slow speed (1 hex per QD) or turn it off and on. Cost: +2 PL, add another +1 per increase in move speed. Drifting: The item will not really be fixated, but will slightly drift. Count as 1 point of corruption. Reversed Gravity: The item will not really be fixated, it will just be repelled away from the ground, just like if it had a negative mass. Unless secured or at all times controlled, it will fly off into space. Count as up to 2 points of corruption.

Unstable: The effect is not so permanent Roll a [[/r 1d6]], it only lasts for this long. 1: [[/r 2d6]] days, 2: [[/r 2d6]] weeks, 3: [[/r 2d6]] months, 4: [[/r 2d6]] years, 5-6: Never, it is actually stable. The GM makes this roll in secret. Count as 1 point of corruption.

You can make one arrow per PL fly out from a quiver or the like within arm’s reach and then either float slightly before you or slightly above you. Make a resource die roll for arrows and double the risk of depleting the resource per added arrow (PL). The arrows can whenever you need them to, as a fast action be launched towards any target within L range. Make a marksmanship roll and add an extra x. These attacks have a base damage of two. Any targets are allowed to parry or dodge the attacks as if they were a ranged attack made from a bow. Armor rating will also protect against the damage.

You can heat up your victim’s blood to the point where he literally bursts into flames. The spell inflicts damage to STR equal to the PL and keeps inflicting 1 point of damage per round until the victim puts the fire out with a successful MOVE roll (slow action). Armor does not protect against this spell.

You fall into a deep sleep and enter a state of unawareness for the duration of the ritual, during which nothing can awake you. Once the ritual ends, you gain a number of WP equal to twice the PL and it also counts as both rest and sleep. Hibernate must take at least a QD to cast or it has no effect. It cannot be cast more than once per day.

Your mind tells your body to overcome its limitations for one QD per PL. You roll your full attribute dice even when they are damaged. You may push endurance rolls any number of repeated times, even if an effect says that you normally cannot push them even once. When you become broken in STR or AGI, you may on your upcoming initiative make one healing roll on yourself as a slow action.
Manipulating the element of Earth, you cover your body with a layer of living stone, protecting you against damage. You receive an Armor Rating equal to twice the PL.

system.ingredient: A mirror or polished piece of metal
system.description: You can create an illusion and control it with your mind. The illusion looks and acts according to your will, but is completely immaterial, has no scent, and leaves no trace. Everyone who sees the illusion can make an INSIGHT roll to understand that it is an illusion. Each additional PL adds –1 to the roll. Anyone who touches the illusion immediately sees through it. In order to maintain the illusion, the caster must concentrate on it and cannot perform any other actions. More complex illusions require a higher PL. A motionless illusion of a wall requires PL 1, but creating a convincing illusion of a person running around the corner of a house might require PL 3. The GM determines the PL required based on the description of the illusion.

On ground made of dirt, sand or stone, arms made from the very same earth rises up to grasp your target, who must succeed a might roll with a negative modification equal to the PL or become grappled, dropping all held items and falling to the ground. A caught target must break free from the hands, the hands then count as having a melee skill equal to twice the PL. A victim that has not broken free after a turn is dragged under and swallowed by the ground.

You let the unrelenting cold of death seep into your victim. The victim becomes COLD, immediately suffering 1 point of damage to both STR and WIT as a result. The victim continues to suffer 1 point of damage to these attributes each round, until the total amount of damage (to each attribute) equals the PL. The spell has no effect on monsters.

As long as you are on solid ground not made out of sandstone, limestone or marble, you can call forth a small kind of smokeless lava vent, no bigger than a camp fire. It will provide all the benefits of a camp fire and will warm you, if you are cold over the duration. Lasts for 1 QD per PL.
The symbol awakens a deep fear in the victim, who suffers damage to WIT equal to the PL. No effect on monsters.

Your drain the will to stay awake from your targets. Each PL causes 1 point of damage to AGI. You can distribute the damage across as many opponents as you want. The targets may attempt to resist the effect by rolling for insight – each x rolled negates 1 point of damage. On a failed roll the targets become sleepless. No effect against monsters.

You call a bolt of lightning from the sky to strike the target, as long as you both are outdoors on a cloudy day. The lightning strike is delayed [[/r 1d6]] rounds unless it is raining, if so, the attack is immediate. The GM makes any such roll in secret. After any eventual delay, the main target of your attack suffers damage equal to the PL. Also, roll for an attack against everyone within N range of the main target (in the same zone) with a number of Base Dice equal to the PL. If anyone loses at least half their STR from the damage, they also fall prone. Objects vulnerable to fire catches fire. Only metal armor will protect against the damage. Why does metal protect against lightning spells? Human bodies are great at conducting electricity, so much that lightning travel through the ground often has an easier way forward by travelling up one leg and down another. Bodies also conducts better than water, and that makes electricity very dangerous while submerged. One way of reducing this is to give the electricity something more conductive to travel through instead, like metal armor. Even partial metal armor could help to redirect the electricity past one’s heart and brain.

The target reduces the potency of all poison and disease suffered during the upcoming QD by 3 per PL. You can also spend PL to add another target to the spell. It does not affect any poisons or diseases that the target may have already contracted, before the spell was cast.

You, or one ally per PL, automatically succeed any swim actions for 1 QD as long as you are not wearing metal armor. All affected can also hold their breath for up to 15 minutes on a successful endurance check. PL can be spent to double the duration, but you still cannot hold your breath during the duration for more than 15 minutes at a time.
You can enhance your hearing magically and hear specific sounds up to D range as clearly as if you stood right where they emanate from. You must see the place to which you direct your hearing.

system.ingredient: Piece of ice or a fistful of snow (optional)
system.description: You summon extreme cold within N range (the same zone). Everyone within the zone makes an ENDURANCE roll or becomes COLD. All water within range immediately freezes.

Special: (POWER WORD; REACTION); Power Word; Reactive.

You can use this spell as a reaction when someone falls. You, or one ally per PL, clothes extends and forms into wings when falling and while you don’t have the STR to fly, all fall damage will be negated. It can be used as a Reaction and/or as a Power Word for one extra PL respectively.

You can get the current hex of anyone object or person as long as they are within 3 hexes from your current location. Each extra PL doubles this range. If you are in the same hex as the thing you are trying to locate, extra PL can instead reveal the direction to it, and/or give you a feeling of the actual distance to it.

You impart some of your talents directly into your targets mind. The targets rank in a profession talent or general talent you have, counts as one higher for the duration. It can only be increased to rank no higher than the PL. The target may at any time before the duration runs out, spend XP to permanently learn the talent, even if they do not meet it normal prerequisites, like if it is from another profession. If you impart a spell discipline, the target can be given access to all the spells you know, during the duration, up to one spell rank higher than their given talent rank. Poking in someone’s mind is delicate, the spell therefor takes a turn (15 minutes) to cast, if you are damaged while casting it, the spell fails and the target suffers a critical horror injury. If this spell suffers a magical mishap, both you and the target suffer the effect of the mishap, if possible.

Must be cast on a sleeping target within range. They must then succeed an insight roll with a penalty equal to the PL or you can completely dictate their actions for the duration of the spell, during which they may interact with others and even throw themselves out of a cliff, if you so want them to. You must instruct them what they should do when you cast the spell. You gain no control of the target after it has been cast. Lasts 1 turn per PL, after that they will awake, if they have not returned to their bed. If they did return to their bed in time, they will not remember that they were sleepwalking.

You stimulate and quicken plant growth in a small area. This can yield you PL units of vegetables, as long as the land can produce editable plants, or speed up the natural progress of vegetation growth in the area by 1 year per PL.

system.ingredient: A handful of crushed lava stones
system.description: As long as the target area is not standing on ground made out of sandstone, limestone or marble, then after 1 turn, a volcanic vent erupts and swallows a building or wall in a fiery inferno. Each added PL can be used to further destroy adjacent stronghold functions. Each PL will also start a random fire. If you use the “Arson event” module under the Stronghold section, that can be used for inspiration for the fires.

You can manipulate an enemy’s blood so that the victim immediately loses consciousness. Resisting the spell requires a successful WIT roll (not an action) with a negative modification equal to the PL. The victim cannot be woken, but wakes up by themselves once the magic wears off. You can also use the PL to affect multiple victims at once – every two steps of increased PL causes the spell to affect an additional victim. For example, PL 3 can affect two victims and PL 5 three victims.
You can focus the forces of nature to enlighten dark souls. You immediately heal a number of WIT or EMP points equal to the PL of your spell. You cannot heal yourself.

system.ingredient: Hair from or part of the victim's body
system.description: You place a blood curse on your victim, who must be a living humanoid. You must know your victim’s name and know where he is, at least approximately. The victim suffers damage to an attribute of your choice. The amount of damage equals the PL and the victim takes 1 point of damage per QD until the full effect is reached.

Your song is charged with so much power that you make the very ground shake and tear. You can use the spell to tear down a wall or fortifications or inflict damage on a victim. The damage caused is equal to the PL.

This spell targets 1 willing subject per PL. Each such target falls into a deep sleep for 15 minutes and when they wake up, they restore 1 point to all attributes, and they also gain 1 WP if their WP is below their current EMP. No target can be affected by healing trance more than once per QD, and if you use the “Short break” module, this counts as a short break.

You can summon a mara and force it to haunt a victim. For attributes and attacks, see Mara in the adventure site Oxengelder (page 194). You decide what form the mara should take, as long as it is not bigger than a human. But the figure is always twisted and terrifying, and a summoned mara always shares some features with the oneiromancer who conjured it. When summoning it, the sorcerer slips into a dream where the victim is visualized for the mara, who immediately goes after them. The sorcerer must have a clear mental image of the victim for the mara to understand who it is supposed to haunt. The mara does everything in its power to attack its victim, and everything it sees the sorcerer can see as well, as long as they remain in the dream. After completing its task, the mara disappears back into the shadows. The sorcerer may choose to wake from the dream at any time, but can never resume contact with the mara.

An animal, bird, reptile, demon, undead, tiny dragon, or extra-large insect is called forth and becomes bound to you as your familiar. They cannot talk, and will not fight for you. You can however use them as the source point for your spells and command them. They can communicate twoword sentences telepathically, this is enough to grant you a +1 modifier to scouting as long as they are nearby. You can also spend a turn (15 minutes), to enter a trance and completely take over their body and senses. During this, others cannot wake you up. A familiar sustain themselves on spirit energy and require no food, but can eat and that can increase their mood. If they die, they are not gone for good, they will return if you recast this ritual at the same PL. You can have a maximum of one familiar, and must be without one for [[/r 1d6]] weeks before you can get a new. The animal can have a total amount of attributes (STR and AGI) equal to 5 + 1 per PL. You can use the Gamemasters Guide page 126 to 127 to see some stats for common animals. You may also add PL to make it more intelligent, making it more communicative, like adding a word to each sentence per PL. You can add two PL to have it gain some basic utility, like a weak fire breath, just enough to light your campfire.

system.ingredient: Your own or the target's blood
system.description: @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.VdFVbDtnUPNnnUv2]{Stir the Blood} 1 @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.JNkvTlEQ9oIBxYjz]{Bind Demon} 2 Blood Bond 2 @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.pV2XXPY9Hx7a1rce]{Immolate} 2 @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.roKVFO8rJcUyKqVi]{Blood Curse} 3 @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.onnFXcdjXEXOQZmy]{Blood Channeling} 3 @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.UWdPQeaD0BwU9JIR]{Bind Soul} 3 ✥ DURATION: Immediate ✥ INGREDIENT: Your own or the target’s blood You can transfer blood, and the inherent energy of it, to or from another being of the same kin as yourself. You can transfer a number of attribute points (of any attribute) equal to the PL to or from the target. The starting attribute rating cannot be surpassed. Attribute points lost in this way can be recovered normally. An unwilling victim can make an INSIGHT roll, with a negative modification equal to the PL, to resist the spell. The spell can be used to get a Broken person up on her feet, but it has no effect on critical injuries.

You can read the surface thoughts of another person for a few minutes. Digging deeper for memories is harder, and requires PL 2 or even more, depending on how fresh the memory is. You can also use this spell to send your own thoughts to another person. In that case, the range of the spell is L if you know the target well. By sending thoughts of pain and suffering, you can inflict damage to WIT or EMP equal to the PL. No effect on monsters.

system.ingredient: Blanket of insects (optional; consumed if available)
system.description: This spell blankets the entire area, which can be a whole settlement and more, in aggressive insects for 1 turn per PL. Anyone in the area is subjected to the effects of a @UUID[Compendium.world.spells.Item.FOU87xWAsMdG6DYJ]{Harass} spell, except that they cannot end it with a successful move roll, as new insects constantly reappear.
